Agnipurāṇa
(also Āgneyap.) one of the 18 Purāṇas; spoken by Agni to Vasiṣṭha; for a. analysis an. account, see JASB. I. p.. 80-86 (Wilson) an. Wilson, Viṣṇup., Preface, p.. lvii. lviii; see also Haraprasad Sastri, Preface to RASB. V. p.. cxlvi ff.
Contains a. account of several branches of learning based on the original treatises of those branches; its account of Viṣṇu's incarnations is based on the Rāmāyaṇa, the M. Bhārata an. the Harivaṁśa; its chs. on medicine, on Suśruta; its chs. on Smṛti, on Yājñavalkya; on the Smṛti chs. in the Agnip., see Kane, HDS. I. p.. 170-3, where the date C. 900 A. D. is given on the basis of the Smṛti chs.; see also IHQ. XII. p.. 689-690; on the Alaṅkāra section in the Agnip., see D., Skt. Poe., I, p.. 102-4, where he assigns the date ‘beginning of the 9th cent.’; also Kane, Intro. to SD., where the date given is C. 900 A. D.; for a. post-Bhoja date for this section, see V. Raghavan, IHQ. X. p.. 767-779 an. Bhoja's Śṛṅgāra Prakāśa (1963) p.. 493-7, 713-7; on the horticultural matter in the Agnip., see Festschrift Moriz Winternitz, p.. 56 ff. (J. J. Meyer); on Bāṇa's (Ist half of 7th cent.) probable use of the Agnip., see Trans. [Page032-a. VI. Ori. Congress. Vol. III. p. 205. For a general survey of its varied contents, see S. D. Gyani, Agni-Purāṇa a Study, 1964.
The above Agnip., taken a. one of the 18 Mahāp. s, is different from the text called by the same name or by the name Vahnip., for the text of which see IO. 3582-3; on this see Our Heritage, Calcutta, I. ii. p.. 209-45; II. i. p.. 77-110.
Many of the Māhātmyas purporting to form part of Agnip. do not occur in an. of the full mss. of the Agnip. (See Wint. HIL. I, p. 566). Some of the sections like the Keralamāhātmya an. those dealing with Paraśurāma seem to belong to a different Āgneyapurāṇa. See above Agastyasaṁhitā (Paraśurāmāyaṇa).
The Agnip. itself gives its extent a. 12000 śls. (ch. 272, 10-11); the Bhāgavata, the Brahmavaivarta an. the Pādma give it 15400 śls.; the Skānda an. the Matsya, 16000; Bik. (p. 183) says nine mss. contain 11000 an. the tenth ms. 12500 śls.; the Ānandāśrama edn. has 383 chs. an. 11457 śls.
In IHQ. XII. p.. 683-689 it is said that the present Agnip. is a recast of a. earlier an. original Agnip. which is the text described by the Matsya an. the Skānda, an. q. by some dharmaśāstra writers. See also Our Heritage, Calcutta, I. ii. p.. 209-45, II. i. 77-110.
